original_question: In which year was the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine awarded to the discoverer of the organelle whose malfunction leads to mucopolysaccharidoses?
key_entities: Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine

final_qi.question: In which year was the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine awarded to the discoverer of the organelle whose malfunction leads to mucopolysaccharidoses?
final_qi.long_answer: The organelle whose dysfunction causes mucopolysaccharidoses is the lysosome. The lysosome was discovered by Belgian cytologist Christian de Duve, who, together with Albert Claude and George Palade, received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1974 for elucidating the structural and functional organization of the cell, including the identification of lysosomes.

final_answer.long_answer: Mucopolysaccharidoses arise from defects in lysosomal enzymes; the lysosome was discovered by Christian de Duve, who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1974 for this discovery and related work on cell organelles.

Mucopolysaccharidoses are lysosomal storage disorders, caused by deficiencies of enzymes that normally reside in the lysosome. The lysosome was discovered by the Belgian cytologist Christian de Duve, who, together with Albert Claude and George Palade, received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1974 for their work elucidating the structural and functional organization of the cell. Hence, the relevant Nobel Prize year is 1974.
